papers.title: (Super-)fast convergence rates for Chernoff approximations via centered differences and Richardson extrapolation
papers.abstract: We use centered differences to construct Chernoff families and derive even asymptotic expansions for their iterated products. Richardson extrapolation is then used to cancel polynomial part and thereby raise the convergence order. As illustrations, we apply the construction to uniformly parabolic, Schr\"odinger-type second-order operators and to a third-order dispersive operator, obtaining, at extrapolation depth $m$, the rates $ O(n^{-2m}) $ on the Sobolev scales $H^{2m+\delta}$, $H^{4m}$, and $H^{5m}$, respectively, with arbitrary $\delta>0$. In the analytic category, quantitative all-order estimates allow the extrapolation depth to grow with the base resolution and yield the super-fast rates $e^{-cn^2}$ for the two second-order models and $e^{-cn} $ for the third-order model. The constructions are explicit in terms of the coefficients of the underlying differential operators and do not use the target semigroup in their definition. This provides a constructive positive answer to the challenge of super-fast Chernoff approximation formulated by Remizov in Problem 30 of arXiv:2410.00416.

papers.title: Riccati Stability Without Auxiliary Matrices
papers.abstract: In the 2004 collection \emph{Unsolved Problems in Mathematical Systems and Control Theory}, Erik Verriest posed the problem of characterizing Riccati stability ``without invoking additional matrices.'' We give such a characterization through a scalar invariant of the resolvent family. The invariant is defined by covariance balances using at most $n^2+1$ frequency--direction pairs. A finite-dimensional separation argument shows that this covariance radius equals the optimal common ellipsoidal norm of the resolvent family. Combined with the strict bounded real lemma, this yields a necessary and sufficient condition for Riccati stability involving only the Hurwitz property of the first matrix and a single scalar inequality. The invariant reduces to the ordinary spectral radius for one matrix, lies between the pointwise spectral-radius and unscaled small-gain levels of the resolvent family, and coincides with the operator-space spectral radius of Shalit and Shamovich for the natural resolvent function space. The main results have been formally verified in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: Weighted and Sobolev Estimates for Fractional Schr\"odinger Operators with Reverse H\"{o}lder Potentials
papers.abstract: We study weighted and Sobolev estimates for two fractional Schr\"odinger operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $n\geq3$ and $0<s<1$. For the additive operator $L=(-\Delta)^s+V$, with a nonnegative, nontrivial potential $V$ belonging to a suitable reverse H\"older class, $RH_q$, we establish a critical-radius form inequality and decay estimates for the semigroup mass. These yield a heat-kernel bound combining polynomial off-diagonal decay with a fixed positive exponent of decay relative to the fractional critical radius $\rho_s$. A decomposition at this scale gives weighted strong-type estimates for the semigroup maximal operator and weighted Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev estimates for $L^{-\alpha/2}$, $0<\alpha s<n$, together with the corresponding endpoint weak-type estimates. The admissible weights satisfy explicit growth restrictions determined by the kernel decay, and the fractional integration order is $\alpha s$. We also consider the spectral operator $Q=(-\Delta+V)^s$. Assuming $V\in RH_{q_1}$ with $n/(1+s)\leq q_1<n$ and classical critical radius $\rho_1(x)\geq1$, we prove that $\nabla Q^{-1/2}$ maps $H^{1-s,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ into $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $1<p\leq p_0$, where $1/p_0=1/q_1-1/n$. By duality, its adjoint maps $L^{p^{'}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ into $H^{s-1,p^{'}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $p_0^{'}\leq p^{'}<\infty$.

papers.title: Some remarks on nonexistence in the Gamow liquid drop model
papers.abstract: In this paper we deal with the celebrated Gamow liquid drop model, namely, for $m>0$, $N\geq 2$ and $\alpha\in (0,N)$, we study the problem \[ \min\Big\{P(\Omega)+ V_\alpha(\Omega) : \Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^N,\;|\Omega|=m\Big\}\,, \] and focus mostly on the nonexistence of minimizers for large masses. First we show that any possible minimizer in the asymptotic regime must satisfy an optimal thickness property. Eventually, in the simplified setting of sets made up as a tiling of cubes, we show that nonexistence occurs for large masses for the whole range of parameters $N\geq 2$ and $\alpha\in (0,N)$.

papers.title: A geometric lower bound for the clamped plate eigenvalue problem in low dimensions and extensions
papers.abstract: We show that the spectrum of the Dirichlet-biLaplacian can be quantitatively bounded from below in terms of the inradius only, for a general open set in dimensions $2$ and $3$. For the same dimensions, we also extend this result to fractional powers $s$ of the Laplacian, with $N/2<s<2$. The resulting estimate comes with a constant having the correct asymptotic behavior as $s$ approaches the two endpoints $N/2$ and $2$. The proofs exploit capacitary techniques in the vein of Maz'ya.

papers.title: Gauge Transforms and Strichartz Estimates for Benjamin--Ono-Type Dirac Equations
papers.abstract: For $T>0$, we consider the Benjamin--Ono-type Dirac equation $$ i\partial_t\psi(x,t) + D(-\Delta)^{\frac{1}{2}}\psi(x,t) = D\,G(\psi(x,t)), \qquad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,T], $$ where $(-\Delta)^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is the fractional Riesz operator, $D$ is the Dirac operator associated with the Clifford algebra of signature $(0,n)$, and $G(\cdot)$ a scalar-valued quadratic nonlinearity. Under a pointwise anti-commutation condition on $\psi$ and a uniform dyadic regularity assumption on its spatial Fourier profile, we construct a unit-modulus gauge map $u$ by $ u=\exp\bigl(-iw\bigr),$ where $w$ is a solution of $Dw=\psi$. Assuming, in addition, the stated regularity and commutation conditions on $w$, we show that the Plemelj components $u_{\pm}=P_{\pm}u$ solve a coupled Schr\"odinger system with gauge nonlinearities $P_{\pm}N(\psi,u)$, where $$ N(\psi(x,t),u(x,t)) = -2P_{-}\!\left[ G(\psi(x,t)) \right]u(x,t). $$ We also obtain a priori estimates for the homogeneous Sobolev seminorms $\dot H^\sigma$ of $\psi(\cdot,t)$, with at most exponential growth on $[0,T]$, together with estimates for $P_{\pm}N(\psi(\cdot,t),u(\cdot,t))$. Combining these bounds with the homogeneous and inhomogeneous Strichartz estimates for the Schr\"odinger system, we obtain, for $n\geq 3$ and every sharp Schr\"odinger admissible pair $(q,p)$, an a priori Strichartz-type estimate for $\psi$ in $L_T^q\dot W_x^{\sigma,p}$, expressed in terms of the initial datum $\psi(\cdot,0)$ and the a priori controls of $\psi$ in $L_T^\infty H_x^{\sigma+1}$ and $L_T^\infty L_x^\infty$.

papers.title: Linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant. An enhanced approach
papers.abstract: The discriminant of a square matrix is defined as a discriminant of its characteristic polynomial. In this paper we provide a description of linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant assuming that the ground field is large enough. Our description generalizes the known results to the case where the field may have a finite cardinality and its characteristic may divide the size of considered matrices. To obtain this description, we extend the approach used in our previous work on the subject and, in addition to that, introduce new invariants for the action of all bijective linear maps preserving a given polynomial, which are on independent interest and could be applied to other problems in the theory of linear preservers.

papers.title: Dimensional transition and spectral instability in lattice Hardy inequalities
papers.abstract: Discretization can change a sharp stability threshold even when the continuum threshold is recovered at infinity. We study this phenomenon for the Hardy inequality on the integer lattice in dimensions at least three: its best coefficient agrees with the continuum value through dimension eight and is smaller from dimension nine onwards. We characterize this transition by the total critical defect, the summable error obtained by testing the lattice operator against the critical continuum power. A theta-function representation proves that the defect is negative and strictly decreasing from dimension nine; explicit positive Hardy remainders establish its positivity in dimensions three through eight. An exact energy identity relates this defect to the energy saved by optimizing the profile outside the neighbours of the origin. This exterior remains stable in dimensions eight and nine, locating the first loss of positivity in its coupling to those neighbours. We give self-contained proofs of both dimensional ranges. We then describe how local attraction creates a negative eigenvalue in a general class of lattice operators with critical inverse-square tails. Its magnitude is exponentially small near the threshold, with both the rate and the multiplicative prefactor determined by zero-energy solutions. The result allows connected finite modifications of the lattice and nonradial corrections to the tail. The same analysis controls the spread of the emerging state and gives a two-dimensional return scale for the associated Markov chain in every ambient dimension.

papers.title: Reverse H\"older Class and Two-Parameter Good-$\lambda$ Inequality over Hausdorff Content
papers.abstract: Classical harmonic analysis is built upon Lebesgue (or more general) measure. Such a framework is remarkably successful for sets of full ambient dimension, but becomes intrinsically insensitive to lower-dimensional geometry: curves, surfaces, and more generally fractal subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\) with zero \(n\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure. In contrast, Hausdorff content provides a dimension-sensitive notion of size for lower-dimensional sets or fractal sets, but harmonic analysis in this setting is still largely limited to maximal operators. In this paper, we establish a weighted two-parameter good-\(\lambda\) inequality under Hausdorff content setting, providing a route toward other general operators from maximal operators over Hausdorff content. To do this, we firstly identify an appropriate reverse H\"older class $\mathcal R\mathcal H_{q,\delta}$ associated with Hausdorff content, and then prove the self-improving property of $\mathcal R\mathcal H_{q,\delta}$ by establishing the fundamental equivalence between reverse H\"older weights and capacitary Muckenhoupt weights. As direct applications, we obtain weighted Fefferman--Stein inequality and some boundedness on general operators over Hausdorff content. The methodology developed in this paper, even when reduced to the Lebesgue measure case, also provide novel insights, which shows that the good-\(\lambda\) principle is not intrinsically tied to an underlying measure, but can extended to a non-additive framework.

papers.title: Bounded Toeplitz operators and unbounded projected multiplication
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth, nonnegative radial symbol $g$ on $\mathbb C$ whose Toeplitz operator on Bargmann--Fock space is positive with singular values decaying faster than every exponential, while projected multiplication $f\mapsto P(gf)$ has no bounded extension from the ambient Gaussian $L^2$ space. All heat transforms of $g$ at positive times are Schwartz functions, and $g\in L^p(dA)$ for every $0<p<2$. We also construct smooth real symbols realizing every possible set of heat boundedness times. Any prescribed positive threshold may be included or excluded, with Schwartz transforms at every later time. All these symbols satisfy the coherent state domain condition, and all heat integrals converge absolutely.

papers.title: Metric gradient flows and variational principles
papers.abstract: We show that Ekeland-type variational principles can be derived from steepest descent curves in metric spaces. From this, we relate the existence of the Calabi flow to the validity of the Ekeland variational principle for the $K$-energy on the space of K\"ahler potentials.

papers.title: Bijective Non-Contractive Maps of Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Spaces Need Not Be Isometries
papers.abstract: Zavarzina asked whether every bijective non-contractive self-map of a precompact quasi-metric space is an isometry. We answer the question in the negative, in a stronger form: on a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space (a tolled extension of the irrational rotation over Z), the shift is a bijective non-contractive map that is not an isometry. The construction generalizes: for every metric space Y, every bijective isometry $\sigma$ of Y, and every point whose $\sigma$-orbit is aperiodic and totally bounded, the tolled Z-extension is such a counterexample; instances include the irrational rotation and the p-adic odometer. The conjugate space is not precompact, so the two-sided hypothesis of Zavarzina's positive result is sharp, and the space is not expand-contract plastic. The core results, including the general scheme and the circle instance, are machine-checked in Lean 4 over mathlib, sorry-free (no unproved steps), under a pinned toolchain. A structural section proves a monochromy theorem: for every strict pair on a hereditarily precompact space, one endpoint's backward self-returns have self-defect at least a quarter of the pair's defect, uniformly on a chain-closed displacement set. Boundary results delimit what remains open: one-sided compactness together with separation.

papers.title: Not too many miles from $\ell_\infty$ to $L_\infty$
papers.abstract: For either real or complex scalars, we improve the known upper bound for the Banach--Mazur distance between $L_\infty[0,1]$ and $\ell_\infty$, proving $d_{\operatorname{BM}}(L_\infty[0,1],\ell_\infty)\leqslant (2+\sqrt5)^2=9+4\sqrt5=17.944\ldots$. The additional input is a stabilised kernel estimate: the copy of $\ell_\infty$ in $L_\infty$ is chosen so that its kernel is an $\ell_\infty$-sum of singular two-point hyperplanes, and Cohen's bound-two construction is then applied coordinatewise. The quantitative part of the proof is an asymmetric Pe\l czy\'nski-type factorisation, with the elementary optimisation included below.

papers.title: Strong-type endpoint obstructions for bilinear spherical maximal operators
papers.abstract: For the bilinear spherical averages in dimension $d\geq2$, we show that the lacunary maximal operator is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^q(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^r(\mathbb R^d)$ whenever $1\leq q\leq\infty$ and $1/r=1+1/q$. The obstruction is realized by fixed nonnegative inputs; a second construction proves quantitative failure on smooth compactly supported functions and finitely many dyadic scales. The same conclusions hold for the full maximal operator. We give a sharp Lorentz-index criterion in the range $q>d/(d-1)$ and extend the negative result to all multilinear spherical maximal operators with an $L^1$ input. We indicate the precise strong-type boundary statements to which these conclusions apply, without drawing conclusions about separate weak-type or interior estimates.

papers.title: Schauder and Riesz Bases for Higher-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces Inspired by ReLU Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Motivated by the role of piecewise linear functions in ReLU neural networks, we study systems of dilated functions in the Lebesgue spaces $L_q([0,1]^d)$, $q\in(1,\infty)$. For a sequence $\tau\in\ell_1$ we consider the operator $T_\tau g(x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty \tau_k g(kx)$ and the function system $\mathcal Z^\tau$ obtained by applying it to the trigonometric system. We show that $\tau\mapsto T_\tau$ is an isomorphism of algebras from $\ell_1$ with the Dirichlet convolution as multiplication onto an algebra of operators and connect the inverse of $T_\tau$ to the inverse of $\tau$ with respect to the Dirichlet convolution. We give explicit conditions on $\tau$, under which the resulting system $\mathcal Z^\tau$ is a Schauder basis of $L_q([0,1]^d)$ and, for $q=2$, a Riesz basis for which we estimate the Riesz constants in terms of $\tau$. We characterise the Riesz bases of this type in terms of a sequence space of Dirichlet convolution multipliers, and we treat mixed systems of cosine and sine functions with different sequences. Finally, we apply these results to the system generated by two piecewise linear functions inspired by ReLU networks and improve the known lower Riesz constant to $2/3$, independently of the dimension.

papers.title: Compact Quasi-Metric Spaces Are Expand-Contract Plastic
papers.abstract: On a totally bounded metric space every non-contractive self-map is an isometry. For quasi-metric spaces, taken $T_1$ throughout ($d(x,y) = 0$ implies $x = y$), this fails: Zavarzina gave a hereditarily precompact counterexample and asked whether bijectivity restores rigidity; a recent example, the toll spiral, shows that it does not. We prove that compactness does: every compact quasi-metric space is expand-contract plastic, that is, each of its bijective non-contractive self-maps is an isometry. Countable compactness suffices, as does compactness of the conjugate topology. Bijectivity cannot be dropped: a compact, hereditarily precompact quasi-metric on the natural numbers makes the shift non-contractive and not an isometry. For arbitrary non-contractive self-maps we prove rigidity when the space is hereditarily precompact and its conjugate topology is sequentially compact, in particular when it is hereditarily precompact and Yoneda complete; neither hypothesis can be dropped. In both theorems the $T_1$ axiom can be weakened to $R_0$ ($d(x,y) = 0$ implies $d(y,x) = 0$), with hereditary precompactness read sequentially (every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence), but not to $T_0$. We construct a $T_0$ space with all the remaining hypotheses of both theorems, Yoneda complete and compact both in its own topology and in the conjugate one, carrying a bijective non-contractive self-map that is not an isometry. Under $R_0$ the two-sided case reduces to the metric theorem, both topologies being sequentially compact exactly when the symmetrized distance is compact; the one-sided theorems do not reduce to it, and plasticity does not pass to the symmetrization even for compact spaces. The two theorems are machine-checked in Lean, and so are the counterexamples, apart from a few statements listed at the end.

papers.title: Fixed points for uniformly asymptotically H\"older-Lipschitz mappings
papers.abstract: In this work, we show that if $K$ is a nonempty, closed, bounded, and convex subset of $X$ and $1\leq \gamma<\sqrt{N(X)},$ where $N(X)$ denotes the Bynum normal structure coefficient, then every uniformly asymptotically H\"older $\gamma$-Lipschitz mapping $T\colon K\to K$ has a fixed point. To achieve this, it was necessary to guarantee the existence of a subsequence of a bounded sequence whose asymptotic diameter is controlled by the quantity $D(\{x_n\}),$ introduced by Jim\'enez-Melado, while simultaneously preserving the asymptotic radii at every point of the closure of the linear span generated by the original sequence. This allowed us to remove the H\"older exponent from the calculations and obtain a H\"older-type extension of the Casini--Maluta, Lim--Xu, and, consequently, Kim--Xu theorems.

papers.title: Products of Berezin Transforms on Generalized Fock Spaces
papers.abstract: We study products $B_{\alpha,m}^{(d)}B_{\beta,m}^{(d)}$ of Berezin transforms on generalized Fock spaces over $\mathbb C^d$. We establish a result for $m\neq2$: if $B_{\alpha,m}^{(d)}B_{\beta,m}^{(d)}$ coincides with another such product, then the weight parameters of the second product must be $(\alpha,\beta)$. As consequences, we characterize when two Berezin transforms commute and when the product of two Berezin transforms is again a Berezin transform.

papers.title: Decomposition of functions of bounded variation in Ahlfors-regular PI spaces
papers.abstract: We prove that, on a non-compact Ahlfors-regular PI space, every function of bounded variation $f$ can be decomposed as a countable sum $\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ of monotone functions of bounded variation $f_n$, in such a way that the total variation of $f$ is the sum of the total variations of the functions $f_n$. Our result extends a Euclidean result of Bianchini and Tonon to the metric setting.

papers.title: Averaged derivatives and reverse inequalities in quasiregular Bergman spaces
papers.abstract: We study weighted Bergman spaces of quasiregular mappings on the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with weight $(1-|x|)^\alpha$, $\alpha>-1$. For every fixed distortion bound $K\ge1$ and every $p>0$, we characterize Bergman integrability by averaged derivatives. We also give geometric conditions under which integration over a subset, or against another measure, controls the full Bergman integral. When $K$ is sufficiently large, the dominating sets are precisely the relatively dense sets. For comparison, we determine the dominating sets for the M\"obius class $K=1$ in dimensions $n\ge3$. At the critical exponent $p=n+\alpha$, its domination criterion differs from that for every fixed $K>1$. Our results extend aspects of the Bergman theory developed by Nolder~\cite{Nolder90} and by Oleinik and Vuorinen~\cite{OV}, and complement the recent work of Adamowicz and Gonz\'alez~\cite{AG21,AG25} and Adamowicz and Caama\~no~\cite{AC} on quasiregular Hardy spaces.

papers.title: There are no unconditional Schauder frames of exponentials in $L^p$ spaces, $p \ne 2$
papers.abstract: We proved recently that there are no unconditional Schauder frames of exponentials in the space $L^p(\Omega)$, $1 \le p < 2$, for any set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of finite measure. For $p > 2$, we proved that the same holds provided that $\Omega$ has nonempty interior, but the general case remained open. In this note we close this gap, i.e., we establish that exponentials cannot form an unconditional Schauder frame in $L^p(\Omega)$, $p \ne 2$, without any additional assumptions on the set $\Omega$ of finite measure other than measurability.

papers.title: An unbounded convex set with the fixed point property for nonexpansive mappings
papers.abstract: We construct an equivalent norm on $\mathbb{R}\oplus\ell_2$ and a nonempty closed convex unbounded subset having the fixed point property for nonexpansive self-mappings. The ambient renormed space has the fixed point property on bounded closed convex subsets. The main point is a geometric localization estimate at a distinguished point of the unbounded set; the fixed point conclusion then follows from the Kirk--Ray localization theorem.

papers.title: Splines and Operators: Part I - Admissibility and Native Spaces
papers.abstract: The variational theory of splines requires a native space: a Hilbert space over which the regularization energy $\|\mathrm{L} f\|_{L_2}^2$ is well defined and the minimum-energy interpolation problem admits a spline solution. In this paper, we characterize the operators $\mathrm{L}$ that enable the construction of such spaces. Our framework is based on the completion of a space $\mathcal{S}$ of test functions in a controlled Gelfand-triple configuration $\mathcal{S}\subset\mathcal{H}\subset\mathcal{S}'$, which we call a Hilbert-Gelfand space. This departs from the classical reproducing-kernel techniques. Our construction is substantially more general, as it supports arbitrary linear operators and singular behaviors, and it recovers the reproducing-kernel setting as a particular case. It is also complete and canonical: the admissibility conditions on $\mathrm{L}$ are necessary and sufficient, and $\mathrm{L}$ determines its native space as the unique Hilbert-Gelfand space on which it extends to a bounded surjection onto $L_2$. We first show that Hilbert-Gelfand spaces are in one-to-one correspondence with compatible Riesz pairs $(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A}^{-1})$ of positive-definite operators $\mathcal{S}\to\mathcal{S}'$. We then extend this correspondence to conditional Riesz pairs, where $\mathrm{A}$ is only conditionally positive-definite, which is the scenario that is relevant to splines. The theory identifies the \emph{attainable null space} of the energy as the unique admissible conditioning, realizes the abstract completions as concrete spaces of distributions, and provides a verifiable admissibility condition in terms of a dual energy functional. The framework is illustrated with the fractional Laplacian, which covers polyharmonic and thin-plate splines, and with ordinary differential operators, which cover exponential splines.

papers.title: Splines and Operators: Part II - Resolution of Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: We present a unified treatment of the data-fitting problems with quadratic (Hilbertian) regularization that arise in approximation theory, machine learning, engineering, and statistics. The generic problem is an optimization in the continuum: given $M$ linear measurements of an unknown function, one minimizes a convex data-fidelity term that is penalized by $\|\mathrm{L} f\|^2_{L_2}$, where $\mathrm{L} $ is a differential-like (spline-admissible) operator. The natural domain of the minimization is the native space $\mathcal{H}_\mathrm{L}$ of $\mathrm{L} $ - the largest Hilbert space over which the regularizer remains meaningful - for which we provide a concise and directly usable characterization. Central to our formulation is a measurement-adapted (conditioned) basis that decouples the null-space and spline components of the solution. This basis serves in three places. First, it tightens the formulation of our representer theorem, which confines the unique solution to an $M$-dimensional space without any orthogonality constraint on the coefficients. Second, it streamlines the implementation, as the exact discretization of the problem becomes an unconstrained convex program with closed-form solutions in the least-squares case, which covers ridge regression, Tikhonov regularization, and smoothing splines. Third, it makes the bridge with the minimum-mean-square-error estimation of generalized Gaussian processes, which is the topic of a companion paper.

papers.title: A proof of Kahane's conjecture in the Wiener algebra
papers.abstract: We prove Kahane's conjecture: if a continuous unimodular function $F$ on the circle satisfies $\|F^n\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}=o(\log|n|)$ as $|n|\to\infty$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, then $F(x)=e^{i(mx+b)}$ for some $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}$. The main step is a logarithmic lower bound for averages: for every nonconstant real-valued $\varphi\in A(\mathbb{T})$, $\frac{1}{T}\int_a^{a+T}\|e^{it\varphi}\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}dt \ge c_\varphi\log T \quad(a\in\mathbb{R},\ T\ge T_\varphi)$, where $c_\varphi>0$ and $T_\varphi>1$ are independent of $a$. The proof uses exact sampling on finite subgroups of the circle, uniformly bounded localized modulations, and the weighted non-harmonic Littlewood inequality of Jaming--Kellay--Saba. A suitable cutoff and a small linear perturbation of the phase ensure that a fixed positive proportion of the coefficients at the beginning of the frequency ordering have modulus one. Passing to integer powers and removing the degree of the circle map yield Kahane's conjecture without any additional smoothness assumptions. We also give equivalent phase, convolution, and operator formulations, and derive consequences for homomorphisms of weighted Wiener algebras and for higher-dimensional tori.

papers.title: A counterexample concerning the coefficient formula for de Branges-Rovnyak norms
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}(b)$ be the de Branges-Rovnyak space associated to a non-extreme point $b$ of the unit ball of $H^\infty$, and let $\phi=b/a$, where $a$ is the Pythagorean mate of $b$. In an earlier article, the author showed that, if $\phi\in H^2$, then \[ f\in\mathcal{H}(b) \iff \Bigl(f\in H^2 \text{ and }\sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty\Bigr), \] in which case we have \[ \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}(b)}^2=\sum_{m\ge0}|\hat{f}(m)|^2 +\sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2. \] It was also shown that there exists a space $\mathcal{H}(b)$ for which $\phi\in\cap_{p<2}H^p$, yet \[ f\in\mathcal{H}(b)\not\Rightarrow \sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty. \] Here we complete this circle of ideas by showing that there exists a space $\mathcal{H}(b)$ for which $\phi\in\cap_{p<1}H^p$, yet \[ \Bigl(f\in H^2\text{ and } \sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty\Bigr) \not\Rightarrow f\in\mathcal{H}(b). \]

papers.title: Dynamical Properties of Perturbed Weighted Shifts
papers.abstract: In this paper, sufficient conditions are established for diagonal perturbations of weighted shifts to be supercyclic, hypercyclic, and frequently hypercyclic, extending several classical results for weighted shifts to this more general setting. In addition, a complete analytic characterization of the shadowing property for these operators is obtained. Consequently, examples of frequently hypercyclic perturbed weighted shifts with the shadowing property are constructed.

papers.title: Integral Representations and Sharp Numerical Radius Inequalities for Hilbert Space Operators
papers.abstract: We study the numerical radius \(\omega(T)\) of a bounded linear operator \(T\) on a complex Hilbert space. Write \(T=A+iB\), where \(A\) and \(B\) are the real and imaginary parts of \(T\). A central result is the exact formula \[ \omega(T)=\frac{\pi}{2}\sup_{\|x\|=1}\int_0^1 \left|\left\langle (A\cos \pi t+B\sin \pi t)x,x\right\rangle\right|\,dt . \] For every \(n\in\mathbb N\), we also prove the power form \[ \omega^{2n}(T)=\frac{4^n}{\binom{2n}{n}} \sup_{\|x\|=1}\int_0^1 \left\langle (A\cos \pi t+B\sin \pi t)x,x\right\rangle^{2n}\,dt . \] This yields sharp upper bounds; for \(n=1\), together with the matching integral lower bound, it recovers Kittaneh's classical two-sided inequality \[ \frac14\|T^*T+TT^*\|\le \omega^2(T)\le \frac12\|T^*T+TT^*\|. \] Furthermore, we obtain exact numerical radius formulas for some block operator matrices, including a \(3\times3\) nilpotent matrix and longer alternating paths. The factor \(\pi/2\) is best possible.

papers.title: Polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille Bounds and Hardy--Littlewood Inequalities for Finite Local Systems
papers.abstract: The complex polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille inequality states that, for a $d$-homogeneous polynomial $P:\mathbb C^N\to\mathbb C$, $P(z)=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}c_\alpha z^\alpha$, the coefficient norm $(\sum_{|\alpha|=d}|c_\alpha|^{p_d})^{1/p_d}$ is bounded by $B_d^{\mathrm{pol}}\|P\|_\infty$, where $p_d=2d/(d+1)$ and $B_d^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is independent of $N$. Here $\|P\|_\infty$ is the supremum norm on the unit polydisc. This inequality has a Boolean analogue for the Fourier--Walsh coefficients of functions of degree at most $d$, with the supremum taken over $\{-1,1\}^N$. In this setting, Defant, Masty{\l}o and P\'erez obtained subexponential bounds, and Ivanisvili established polynomial growth. Further polynomial estimates were obtained by Slote, Tseng and Volberg in the Boolean setting and by Slote and Volberg for cyclic groups. We study these coefficient inequalities in a broader framework of finite systems of functions that encompasses and extends the Boolean and cyclic settings. This framework also admits a natural $\ell_p$ formulation, leading to Hardy--Littlewood-type inequalities. For orthonormal systems, we obtain polynomial bounds for the Bohnenblust--Hille constants and, for sufficiently large $p$, for the constants in these Hardy--Littlewood-type inequalities. In the Boolean case, the polynomial power is $5/2$, with a cubic logarithmic factor.

papers.title: Schatten class membership of products of composition operators and their adjoints
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Schatten class membership of the product of a composition operator and the adjoint of another composition operator on the Hardy and Bergman spaces. We provide several sufficient conditions and necessary conditions for these operators to belong to the Schatten classes. Moreover, for some specific symbols including linear fractional maps, finite Blaschke products, and inner functions, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions.
